Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are Greenport's redlines for the MSA and the Order Form. High level on governing law / dispute resolution: we prefer New York law and arbitration seated in New York (Commercial Arbitration Rules), but we are willing to be flexible if Redwood accepts a clear carve for emergency relief in Greenport's local courts.

Key asks in the redline:
- Governing law: New York (State law).
- Arbitration: binding arbitration for claims > $250k; small claims and injunctive/emergency relief carved out to state courts.
- Emergency relief carve: allow either party to seek provisional relief in any court with jurisdiction to preserve status quo (IP, data, injunctive preservation) prior to arbitration.
- Consent to service for Greenport (we can accept email service if needed).

Please loop in your legal. We're aiming to finalize the Order Form this month so we can kick off the pilot.

Hannah —

Quick read-through attached; high-level thoughts below.

On the split approach: acceptable in principle, but we need to be explicit about two items so the carve doesn't swallow our arbitration:
1) Governing law (choice of substantive law) and arbitral seat (procedural locus) can be different — we can propose Delaware law with an arbitral seat of New York. That keeps the law familiar while keeping procedural consistency.
2) Emergency relief carve must be narrowly drafted: limited to provisional remedies required to preserve evidence, stop imminent data exfiltration, or preserve injunctive relief for IP. Require a short notice window to the other party (except in true emergency) and a requirement to file for arbitration within X days of seeking emergency relief (we normally ask 30 days).

Other negotiation levers: cap the monetary threshold for arbitration trigger (their $250k proposal is fine) and include a stepped dispute ladder (informal escalation + mediation before arbitration) to avoid overuse.

I'll draft language for a counterproposal. Vanessa — if we accept a split with Delaware law, is that a showstopper commercially?

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Melissa —

Thanks for the redlines and context. Please see our counter attached; summary below to keep the thread high-level.

1) Governing law / seat: We propose Delaware substantive law for the MSA and an arbitral seat of New York for arbitration proceedings. We believe this split preserves predictability while keeping arbitration administration local to an efficient venue.

2) Provisional remedies / emergency relief: We will accept a carve that allows either party to seek provisional remedies (injunctive relief, property preservation, or emergency data preservation) in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to the constitution of an arbitral tribunal, but only if all of the following are met:
   - The relief sought is strictly to preserve evidence, to prevent imminent data exfiltration, or to preserve intellectual property;
   - The seeking party provides notice to the other party as soon as practicable (48 hours where feasible);
   - The seeking party must commence arbitration proceedings within 30 days after obtaining provisional relief or the provisional relief will lapse; and
   - Any provisional relief must be narrowly tailored and limited in duration to the minimum necessary to preserve the subject matter.

3) Stepped dispute resolution: we propose an initial 30-day good-faith escalation and mediation step for disputes under $250k to avoid arbitration churn.

Commercially, we can offer a one-time 30-day implementation credit if Greenport accepts the counter without further venue changes. That would help them meet their 11/22 onboarding target.

Please let us know whether Greenport can live with the split and the 30-day filing requirement; if so we can circulate a final clean MSA + Order Form for signature.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
